name: Wei (Warring States)
alt: Wei of the Seven Warring States

predecessors.name: Jin (Chinese state)
predecessors.text: Anyi and the Hedong district, Xihe and the Zhongshan lands that Wei held at the partition

successors.name: Kingdom of Han (Liu Bang)
successors.text: Western Wei, 'southern Shanxi', absorbed into the Han commandery of Hedong in 205

ledger.x: 403: King Weilie of Zhou recognises Wei Si as Marquess of Wei at Anyi.
381: Zhongshan regains its independence from Wei.
376: 'In 376 BC, the states of Han, Wei and Zhao deposed Duke Jing of Jin' and divided the last Jin territory.
361: King Hui moves the capital from Anyi to Daliang (Kaifeng).
328: Zhang Yi leads Qin against Wei.
328: Qin acquires 'a large part of Wei'.
328: the fight for Xihe ends in Qin's favour.
293: Qin breaks Han and Wei at Yique.
286: Qin takes Anyi, the former Wei capital.
286: the Qin-Wei fight for Hedong ends with Anyi.
275: Qin chancellor Wei Ran besieges Daliang; Wei is 'forced to cede eight cities' (unnamed) and 'persuaded Wei Ran to accept the cession of Wenyu (present-day Wen County)'.
225: Wang Ben floods Daliang and Wei surrenders to Qin.
208: Wei is restored after the Qin collapse (Wei Jiu, then Wei Bao).
206: Xiang Yu keeps the Wei lands of Henan for Western Chu.
206: Wei Bao is made King of Western Wei.
205: Han Xin captures Wei Bao and Western Wei ends.

wars.name: Wei's conquest of Xihe
wars.outcome: Wei victory: General Wu Qi 'occupied Qin territory to the east of the Luo River for the four years between 409 and 406 BCE'; Xihe Commandery was set up after the capture of five cities (undated).

wars.name: Wei's conquest of Zhongshan
wars.outcome: Wei victory: 'in 407, Zhongshan was conquered by Wei troops, led by general Yue Yang' (Zhongshan page, 'conquered in 407-406'); the Marquess Wen page: 'The state of Zhongshan was eliminated in 406 BCE'; the siege lasted three years (undated).

wars.name: Zhongshan's independence from Wei
wars.outcome: 'in 381, Zhongshan won its independence back'; Lingshou became its capital in 380.

wars.name: Battle of Maling
wars.outcome: Qi victory: 'the battle of Maling checked Wei's ambitions'.

wars.name: Qin's 328 campaign against Wei
wars.outcome: Qin victory: Zhang Yi's campaign by which Qin acquired a large part of Wei.

wars.name: Battle of Yique and the loss of Hedong
wars.outcome: Qin victory: Yique (293), 400 li of Hedong conceded (290), Anyi taken (286); in 273 Wei ceded 'Nanyang' to Qin 'forcing Wei to seek an armistice' after the Wei-Zhao attack on Han's Huayang (the page does not locate Nanyang).

wars.name: Qin's conquest of Wei
wars.outcome: Qin victory: Wang Ben flooded Daliang and King Jia surrendered; Qin made the Dang and Sishui commanderies.

wars.name: Han Xin's conquest of Western Wei
wars.outcome: Han victory: Wei Bao, who had gone back to Chu in 205, was defeated and captured in October-November 205.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page; Wei's frontiers with Qin (the Yellow River and Hedong), Han, Zhao and Qi are approximate, and the corrected shapes are discs around the named places.
